abstract:
Sepsis carries high morbidity and mortality, and early precise intervention is critical for improving outcomes. The heterogeneity of circulating immune cells, particularly at the monocyte subset level, remains a major barrier to early risk stratification. This study aimed to identify prognosis-associated monocyte subsets and their key regulators in early sepsis, providing potential clues for early prognostic assessment and targeted intervention.
We analyzed single-cell transcriptomic profiles of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from patients with early sepsis and healthy controls in the GSE167363 dataset to define myeloid subsets associated with clinical outcomes. Core regulatory molecules were prioritized by intersecting differentially expressed genes (DEGs) with cell death-related gene sets, and their expression patterns were examined in bulk transcriptomic cohorts. The lead candidate was further evaluated through in vitro functional experiments and in vivo survival studies using the cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) mouse model.
A transitional monocyte subset defined by high CD14 and modest FCGR3A expression, positioned at the intermediate node of monocyte differentiation, was markedly depleted in sepsis non-survivors. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) revealed ferroptosis as the predominant cell death modality in this subset among non-survivors. Lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA) was pinpointed as a core regulatory molecule, and its differential expression was validated in independent bulk transcriptomic cohorts. In vitro assays confirmed that LDHA inhibition attenuated ferroptosis in THP-1-derived macrophages. Consistently, both myeloid-specific Ldha conditional knockout (cKO) and pharmacological inhibition of LDHA markedly improved the 7-day survival of CLP-induced septic mice.
This study identifies an outcome-associated monocyte subset with a ferroptosis signature in early sepsis and suggests a potential regulatory role for LDHA in monocyte ferroptosis.
